task_instance: Build and run a minimal autoresearch-style agent harness per the skill's 'Autoresearch-Style Loop' pattern: a locked evaluator (evaluate.py, scored against a fixed hidden target, integrity-checked by verify_locked.py), an editable surface (config.json), an append-only durable log set (THREAD.md, logs/results.tsv, logs/rejected.md), and a git-based checkpoint/rollback loop (loop.py) that runs 8 iterations, keeps improvements, discards/rolls back regressions, and writes a final proposal (proposals/best_config.json) for human review.
evidence: Work done in research-run/ under the scratchpad exec_div directory. Created evaluate.py (locked, fixed TARGET={a:3,b:-2,c:5} scalar metric), verify_locked.py (sha256 lock/anti-tamper gate), config.json (editable), and loop.py implementing read-locked-context -> propose edit -> git commit checkpoint -> run evaluator -> log -> keep/discard+rollback -> repeat, per the skill's required pattern and file layout (THREAD.md, logs/results.tsv, logs/rejected.md, proposals/). Ran `python3 loop.py` for 8 iterations inside a git repo (git init/commit per iteration). Verified: (1) logs/results.tsv has one row per iteration with config/score/best_score/decision/commit columns and shows 3 keeps and 5 discard_rollback decisions with monotonically improving best_score (-38 -> -34.26 -> -30.27 -> -26.36); (2) logs/rejected.md lists every discarded attempt with the score it lost to and the commit it was rolled back to; (3) THREAD.md is a durable human-readable handoff log narrating every iteration and naming the next agent action (a pruning round); (4) `diff` confirmed the final config.json on disk exactly matches proposals/best_config.json (the git rollback logic correctly restores the best-known state after a worse trial, rather than leaving a regressed config in place); (5) `git log --oneline` shows one commit per iteration plus the init commit, giving cheap rollback and full audit trail; (6) tamper test: edited evaluate.py's TARGET constant, ran verify_locked.py and got 'EVALUATOR TAMPERED: expected <hash> got <hash>' with exit code 1 (metric-gaming detection works), then `git checkout -- evaluate.py` restored it and verify_locked.py printed LOCK_OK with exit code 0. All of this used only python3's standard library and git, both already installed, with zero network access.
